scope: The movement and what it divided into: William Miller's lectures computing the end 'about the year 1843' (Boston, 1842); The Western Midnight Cry, the Millerite paper of the West (1843–44); the first number of Samuel S. Snow's The True Midnight Cry (Haverhill, 22 August 1844), which fixed the day at the tenth day of the seventh month, 22 October 1844; and two of the bodies that formed after the day passed, the Sabbatarian Adventists, in Joseph Bates's The Seventh Day Sabbath, a Perpetual Sign (second edition, New Bedford, 1847), and Ellen G. White's first visions in her Sketch of the Christian Experience and Views (Saratoga Springs, 1851). A Word to the 'Little Flock' (1847) was found only in a facsimile with a later foreword and is not seated. The Advent Christian and other non-Sabbatarian Adventist bodies, and the Midnight Cry and Advent Herald of New York and Boston: QUEUED.
why_seated: The third tradition of 1844: the Millerites expected the return of Christ on 22 October 1844, and the Great Disappointment of that day divided them; the Sabbatarian Adventists, from whom the Seventh-day Adventist Church formed, are one of the bodies that came out of it.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 27 October 2026: "need to seat the book of mormon but im not doing it without several diverging simultaneous traditions in the batch" — offered the traditions that divided in 1844 (the Latter Day Saint succession, the Bab's declaration, the Millerite disappointment, the Taiping beginnings), or the Book of Mormon's own editions — "1. definitely. lets go."
